members.ts: pair: ((key: string, record: Record) => string) | null
change: the listener's first argument, Change
commit: the listener's first argument, Change
raised: the listener's first argument, Raised
handed: the listener's first argument, the ConformancePeer it hands

types.what: the first custom component: a TypeScript object its element holds at conformanceComponent, an EventTarget heard by addEventListener and removeEventListener; its Choice is the app's enum Choice, whose Minimum and Maximum are held as low and high under JsonStringEnumMemberName (D7.7, D9.13)

behaviors.behavior: Calls counts the component's method calls, which it shows; Total() answers its Count, and Check() answers its Enabled.
Settle() awaits the test app's settle endpoint, resolves on its success and rejects when it answers a 500 the harness seeds.
After each raise the component shows Raised and its count of raises, Raised 1 and on.
The component shows NullableCount in its nullable count line, none for null.

The component writes a line into its log, a list named Log with an item for each line, for each value it receives: Date and the value's local yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, TakeMoment's toISOString, null, same record when Take receives the object Snapshot() returned, or text and the text, Log's own text among them.
TakeNullable shows Took and the count it receives, Took none before a call; TakeText shows the text it receives as its taken text, (null) for null and (undefined) for undefined.

Its own Ask button asks Answer for each item and shows the answers in its answer line, each item's position when Answer holds no function; a write that changes Text asks Answer again before the line draws; a throw from Answer leaves the line it drew and shows the message in its error line.
Its own Ask button calls Pair with the key count and each record, and draws each answer in its answer line.
SortItems orders and redraws its items by the key its answer gives for each; SortBy orders its records by the member the field names; the component lists its records' names.
Its own box: Raise raises Raised with the box's text as Text and, when the text reads a number, as Count, and on net10 as Time.

The Raise buttons the test's render options name raise Raised with the payload each names: no text, no optional text, a null nullable text, a record or none, Flag true or false, or no argument; the component shows its payload line once its listeners return.

Its Raise button hands its peer, the same peer at each click, Raise with a new peer puts a new peer on a new element and hands it, Hand a peer raises Handed with its peer, and Drop the peer removes that peer's element and lets go of it.

The render helper takes the items and records the component holds, its Days in the live form (D7.7), an item that lacks a declared member among them, and whether Current() and MaybeItem() answer an item.

Its own controls: a day field setting Day or NullableDay; a list of none, residential and nursing picked with the arrow keys and Enter, setting Value and raising change; Low, High and Hold medium setting Choice, medium a text no value of Choice is held as; Hold 129 setting Days to 129, a number no value of CareDays names; Sort and Edit first over Records; Deactivate last over Items; Paged and Clear over NullableRecords; Free and Busy setting Count to 1 and 0; Destroy; Remove the read-only text.
Add adds the amount it is passed to Amount, which the component shows in a status named Amount.
On the page that names it, the component's own code sets its Binding's Count to a promise.
A script of the test app builds the component only when the page's Build the component button is clicked.

promise.page: A form of two entries, each a ConformanceComponent bound to Entries[i].Code, whose ReactiveValidator writes NotEmpty on each entry's Code, and a Save button.
promise.gesture: Click Pick a-1 in the first component, then click Save.
promise.outcome: The message shows beside the second component only, and nothing is sent.
promise.opposite: With a-1 picked in the first and a-2 in the second, Save sends Entries[0].Code=a-1 and Entries[1].Code=a-2.
promise.defect: The rule is bound to Entries.Code without the index, so the message shows beside the first component.

promise.page: A form whose first entry is rendered by Html.PartialFor(m => m.First), its ConformanceComponent bound to Code under the prefix First, with NotEmpty on First.Code.
promise.gesture: Click Pick a-1 in the first entry's component, then click Save.
promise.outcome: The form sends First.Code=a-1 and the server binds it, showing Saved a-1.
promise.opposite: Saving with no value picked shows the message beside the first entry's component.
promise.defect: The component's name drops the prefix, so the form sends Code=a-1 and the server binds no first code.
